web_evidence.title: Angels & Demons | Dan Brown Official Website
web_evidence.note: Authorized excerpt spanning the prologue and Chapters 1–5 consistently narrates Leonardo Vetra, Langdon, and the killer externally in third person; first person is confined to speech or rendered thought.

web_evidence.title: The Thriller Genre in Dan Brown's Novel Angels and Demons
web_evidence.note: Scholarly analysis explicitly identifies the novel as third-person omniscient and explains that its chapters shift focus among Langdon, Vittoria, the Hassassin, and other characters.

web_evidence.title: Dan Brown Writing Styles in Angels & Demons
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly describes the whole novel as third-person omniscient and notes its chapter-to-chapter shifts among multiple characters.

person_note: The quote set is overwhelmingly dialogue or aphoristic material and therefore cannot vote by its visible I, we, or you pronouns; the sole event quote remains unmarked in isolation. The authorized multi-chapter opening nevertheless shows a nonparticipating third-person narrator across several focal characters, and whole-book scholarly and study-guide analyses independently describe the same third-person structure. Character speech and direct thought are local embedded voices, not alternating base narration. The main uncertainty is the poor diagnostic coverage of the supplied quotes, but the convergent strong web evidence resolves the book as THIRD.
